Numbers.title: Numbers & time
Numbers.subtitle: Numbers, dates, clock times and prices: learn them, then drill them.

cardinals.rule: From 21 on, German says the ones first and the tens second, joined by und: 21 is ein·und·zwanzig (“one-and-twenty”). Watch the spelling: 16 sechzehn and 17 siebzehn lose letters, and so do 60 sechzig and 70 siebzig. 30 is dreißig with ß. Write each number as one word.
cardinals.hundredNote: 100 can be hundert or einhundert, 1000 can be tausend or eintausend. After the hundreds you simply continue: 101 is hunderteins, 321 is dreihunderteinundzwanzig.
cardinals.converterInvalid: Please type a whole number from 0 to 9999.

ordinals.title: Ordinal numbers 1–31
ordinals.rule: Up to 19 add -te: vierte, fünfte, zehnte. Four are irregular: erste, dritte, siebte, achte. From 20 add -ste: zwanzigste, einunddreißigste. In dates the ordinal needs an adjective ending: -e after der (der dritte), -en after am (am dritten).
ordinals.written: In writing, put a dot after the number: 3. November.

calendar.articleNote: All months, weekdays and seasons are masculine: der Januar, der Montag, der Sommer.
calendar.todayNote: The calendar starts on today's date.

clock.noEveryday: Everyday German only uses 5-minute steps. Move the minute to a multiple of 5.
clock.tip: halb means “half before”: halb drei is 2:30, not 3:30. halb and Viertel vor always look at the next hour.

v2.title: The verb comes second (V2)
v2.body: In a German statement the conjugated verb is always the second element. The first element can be the subject or something else, such as the time. If something else comes first, the subject moves behind the verb.

question.title: Asking questions
question.body: In a W-question the question word is first, then the verb, then the subject. In a yes/no question the verb is in first position.

modal-bracket.title: Modal verbs and the sentence frame
modal-bracket.body: The conjugated modal verb stands in position 2. The second verb stays in the infinitive and goes to the very end. Together they form a frame (Satzklammer) around the rest of the sentence.

separable-bracket.title: Separable verbs and the sentence frame
separable-bracket.body: In a main clause the verb stem is in position 2 and the separated prefix goes to the very end. The two parts frame the sentence (Satzklammer).

subordinate-weil.title: weil sends the verb to the end
subordinate-weil.body: After weil the clause is a subordinate clause: the conjugated verb moves to the end of that clause. A comma separates it from the main clause.

negation-nicht-kein.title: Negation with nicht and kein
negation-nicht-kein.body: Use kein to negate a noun that has ein or no article. Use nicht to negate a verb or the whole sentence; it usually stands at the end.

time-manner-place.title: Time – Manner – Place
time-manner-place.body: When a sentence has several details, the usual order is Time (when), Manner (how), Place (where). The verb still stays in position 2.
